subject: mcc-health-promotion
title: HIV prevention: PrEP and PEP

steps.tx: **Pre-exposure prophylaxis**, or PrEP, is offered to HIV-negative people at ongoing risk so they take **antiretrovirals** before any exposure. In India, the national programme supports daily **tenofovir disoproxil with emtricitabine** as the usual combination. Confirm HIV-negative status before starting, and repeat HIV testing at regular intervals while on treatment. Protection depends on taking the tablet every day.

steps.tx: Monitor **renal function** with **creatinine** and urinalysis, because tenofovir can injure the proximal renal tubule. A transient rise should be repeated before any change is made. A persistent fall in kidney function, judged by a sustained decline in **eGFR**, prompts review of the regimen. Hepatitis B coinfection needs particular care, since both drugs treat hepatitis B and abrupt withdrawal can trigger a flare.

rows: Do not stop abruptly; refer for HBV care

steps.tx: **Post-exposure prophylaxis**, or **PEP**, is a short course of **antiretroviral** drugs started after a single possible exposure to HIV. It should begin as early as possible, and the window is limited, so delay is harmful. The regimen is a fixed combination recommended by national guidance, and the first dose should not wait for test results. A **baseline HIV test** is drawn at the same visit, and **follow-up testing** is arranged later to confirm the outcome.

nodes.label: Start PEP as early as possible
Baseline HIV test, no delay to dose

steps.tx: **Acute HIV** can occur in someone on PrEP. Fever, rash, myalgia and generalised lymphadenopathy after a recent exposure suggest seroconversion. In the window period the antibody test can be non-reactive, so **HIV RNA viral load** testing is needed. Missed doses and adherence should be explored, because PrEP failure is usually linked to inconsistent use.
steps.say: Acute HIV can occur in someone taking PrEP. Fever, rash, muscle pain and generalised lymphadenopathy after a recent exposure suggest seroconversion. During the window period the antibody test can be non-reactive, so HIV RNA viral load testing is needed. Explore missed doses and adherence, because PrEP failure is usually linked to inconsistent use.

steps.tx: Sustained **viral suppression** on antiretroviral therapy prevents sexual HIV transmission, a principle called undetectable equals untransmittable. The usual threshold is an undetectable viral load maintained for at least six months. Condoms still protect against other sexually transmitted infections, so keep counselling, testing and adherence support in place for both partners.
